basis: Elbow hypertrichosis and disproportionate short stature define syndrome; aphasia, mutism and echolalia occur in 30-79%, supporting neurologic involvement.
Skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; cardiac anomalies are variable, with no established frequency supporting inclusion across the group.
Immune-mediated inflammatory disease of the intestine; no common direct extraintestinal damage is established for this subtype.
Immune-mediated inflammatory demyelination of the central nervous system; absence of anti-MOG antibodies does not change the affected organ or mechanism.
Aniridia, microcornea and cataract are intrinsic ocular abnormalities.
Malignancy of the uterine endometrium, a reproductive organ outside the axes; metastatic organ damage is not established as common.
NMJ disease; ptosis/ophthalmoplegia in 100% of reported subsets; scoliosis/hyperlordosis 40-50%. Respiratory muscle weakness does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Intellectual disability, ocular malformations and hypogonadism characterize syndrome; muscle atrophy/hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%; cardiac anomalies are under 30%.
Hereditary peripheral sensory nerve dysfunction causing episodic pain; upper-body pain does not establish damage to other organs.
Hemoglobin variants affect red-cell oxygen transport and may cause compensated hemolytic anemia.
Malignancy of lymphoid blood cells; lymphoma requires the immune mechanism axis. No specific extranodal organ is commonly affected across the umbrella.
Inherited retinal degeneration with impaired visual acuity, visual-field constriction and macular changes.
Developmental impairment/hypomyelination core; hearing loss ~50-80%, foot deformities ~70%, GH deficiency ~60%. Common ocular abnormalities omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Skeletal and skin connective-tissue defects define disease; dental abnormalities and global developmental delay each 30-79%. Blue sclerae alone do not establish ocular damage.
Disordered epidermal keratinization; ancestry and subtypes establish skin as the affected organ.
Corneal thinning and ectasia cause reduced visual acuity.
Abnormal cysteine/glycine peptide handling supports a metabolic disorder; intellectual disability frequency is unspecified, and urinary excretion alone does not establish renal damage.
Carcinoma originates in the lung; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Parathyroid malignancy usually causes PTH excess; nephrocalcinosis and osteoporosis each occur in 30-79%, reflecting renal calcium deposition and bone loss.
Frontal cortical malformation causes developmental impairment and spastic paresis; motor deficits arise from brain disease.
Primary skeletal muscle necrosis, weakness and rhabdomyolysis; elevated creatinine or transaminases alone does not establish renal or hepatic damage.
Epithelial tumor of the ovary, a reproductive organ; no endocrine dysfunction or common direct damage to an included organ is established.
Benign vascular tumor or malformation arising from abnormal venous connections; no other anatomical site is specified.
Inherited degeneration primarily affecting the retinal pigment epithelium; neurological ancestry does not establish extraocular nerve disease.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and precocious puberty define the phenotype; puberty occurs in 80-99%. Small hands/feet and uncomplicated hypermobility do not establish skeletal damage.
